answer: Trust propagates from honest anchors through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with each step normalized by node degree. For a sybil set S, low conductance—few crossing edges relative to its volume—limits walk flow entering it; under capped degrees and fixed anchor weight, this bottleneck and min-cut transitivity bounds its aggregate voting weight. An atlas of attestations may contain basalt-like clusters, but an echo of internal sybil links cannot create external trust.
